Name: Auto Hauling
Description:
[h2]Auto Hauling[/h2]

Ever opened a derelict, zoomed out over a cargo-strewn deck, and wondered why perfectly useful supplies were still waiting for someone to notice them one tiny batch at a time? Well, have I got an aggressively organized clipboard for you!

Auto Hauling finds eligible loose cargo and asks Stardeus to create its normal Store tasks for everything it can find in the current scan. It never teleports cargo, invents destinations, or force-assigns workers: Stardeus still owns jobs, storage filters, priorities, pathfinding, safety, retries, and completion.

[h2]Features[/h2]

[h3]All-at-Once Store Assignment[/h3]
- Scans Core's active loose-object collection every 300 game ticks
- Requests ordinary vanilla Store tasks without imposing a small Auto Hauling batch limit
- Leaves reservations, carried cargo, unavailable objects, and Forbidden items alone
- Respects current vanilla storage compatibility before requesting work
- Starts with master automation disabled by default
- Stops automation when disabled without cancelling active vanilla tasks

[h3]Core-Managed Worker Bidding[/h3]
- Stardeus now rotates workers and indexed tasks and tries alternative candidates when bids compete
- Auto Hauling's former idle-worker assist is retired as of 1.1.5
- Core manages jobs, worker eligibility, priorities, safety, reachability, and assignment
- Controls explains the change; existing saved assist preferences are retained for compatibility and have no gameplay effect

[h3]Stalled Store Task Refresh[/h3]
- Optionally refreshes eligible ordinary cargo Store tasks from any creator after more than two continuous in-game days waiting unassigned in Core's bidding state
- Cancels only work Auto Hauling is currently permitted and able to recreate through the same vanilla Store-order path
- Preserves the previous task priority
- Never touches assigned or active work, priority-0 or restricted-worker tasks, Optimization Mod dormant tasks, or unrelated jobs that merely use the Hauling skill
- Rechecks item settings, storage, availability, Intelligent Recycling, Part Restoration Unit, quality, body, mind, and special-target rules immediately before cancellation
- Restores only a material pile's pre-existing allowed state when Core's cancellation itself applies Forbidden
- Reports found, cancelled, and successfully requeued counts in Controls

[h3]Cooperative Quality Ownership[/h3]
- Optionally discovers Intelligent Recycling's read-only API without a compiled dependency
- Requires contract 1, per-object capability 128, and both positive release properties before a quality-bearing object can reach Auto Hauling's settings and vanilla checks
- Re-queries every quality object at the decision point so ownership changes take effect
- Leaves every quality object alone when Intelligent Recycling is absent, initializing, incompatible, unavailable, or uncertain
- Shows conspicuous red notices when the quality lane is unavailable while confirming that non-quality hauling still works
- Never copies processor thresholds or recreates Intelligent Recycling's ownership policy
- Optionally asks Part Restoration Unit whether a quality-bearing body part is released for external automation

[h3]Granular Cargo Controls[/h3]
- Enables every eligible item by default underneath the master switch
- Enables or disables complete generic cargo categories
- Supports individual item overrides inside any category
- Searches by item name, category, or internal definition ID
- Organizes large definition lists with collapsible and nested collapsible sections
- Uses theme-aware managed tabs, vertical scrollbars, and disclosure indicators through AUMF 1.4.0
- Stores the master, stale-refresh, category, and item settings with the save

[h3]Failure Diagnostics[/h3]
- Tracks vanilla Store tasks requested by Auto Hauling, including refreshed replacements
- Retains the most recent 50 failures with item, position, Core reason, task state, attempt count, and retry status
- Does not misreport interrupted or cancelled tasks as failures
- Does not force its own retry behavior; Stardeus remains responsible for retries
- Keeps routine task and API outcomes inside the in-game interface instead of flooding Player.log

[h3]Manual Forbidden Cleanup[/h3]
- Includes a deliberate Allow Forbidden Loose Cargo button and optional user-assigned AUMF shortcut
- Removes every currently detected loose material/object Forbidden flag, including flags on quality, special-target, or mind-associated objects
- Never runs automatically and does not create or cancel a task by itself
- Warns that the action may allow vanilla systems or other mods to process those objects afterward

[h2]Safety and Mod Compatibility[/h2]

Auto Hauling never alters Quality, invents a threshold, forces a destination, changes a being's jobs, or cancels assigned or active work. Worker bidding is managed entirely by Core. Items with no compatible storage are counted and left alone. If a Store task later fails, Auto Hauling retains Core's reason in its in-game Failures tab without taking ownership of retry behavior.

The following remain outside automatic Store-task creation:
- Quality-bearing material piles
- Hullpiercers, Storage Capsules, and Artillery Fungus handled as Intelligent Recycling special targets
- Whole biological or mechanical Beings and bodies
- Mind-bearing and mind-associated objects

Whole-Being hauling remains out of scope because Core's multi-selection Morgue/Mechuary actions already provide a concise manual workflow. Ordinary loose quality-bearing storable objects cross the creation boundary only when Intelligent Recycling reports both ReleasedForAutoHauling and CanCurrentlyBeHauled. When Part Restoration Unit is installed, quality-bearing body parts additionally require its ReleasedForExternalAutomation decision.

[h2]Requirements[/h2]

Requires [b]Auto Utilities Mod Framework 1.4.0[/b]. AUMF provides the cooperative top-bar widget, managed resizable panel, compatibility handshake, guarded persistent shortcut, theme-aware tabs, managed vertical scrollbars, and collapsible sections. Auto Hauling remains inactive when that control surface is unavailable or incompatible.

Intelligent Recycling and Part Restoration Unit are optional. Neither is required for ordinary non-quality Auto Hauling.

[h2]In Short[/h2]

You choose the eligible cargo. Companion mods retain their ownership lines. Stardeus chooses the worker, route, and destination. Auto Hauling fills the list and refreshes safe stalled Store tasks. Core's scheduler puts the crew to work.

[b]Everything gets asked. Nothing crosses the safety boundary.[/b]
